definition: Being moved by another person's suffering together with the wish to relieve it.
taxonomy: BFAS Compassion aspect (DeYoung) · Compassion Scale (Pommier) · Strauss five-element definition
formal_1: Strauss C, Lever Taylor B, Gu J, Kuyken W, Baer R, Jones F & Cavanagh K (2016). What is compassion and how can we measure it? A review of definitions and measures. Clin Psychol Rev 47:15-27. DOI:10.1016/j.cpr.2016.05.004 PMID:27267346 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Pommier E, Neff KD & Tóth-Király I (2020). The development and validation of the Compassion Scale. Assessment 27(1):21-39. DOI:10.1177/1073191119874108 PMID:31516024 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: DeYoung CG, Quilty LC & Peterson JB (2007). Between facets and domains: 10 aspects of the Big Five. J Pers Soc Psychol 93(5):880-896. DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.93.5.880 PMID:17983306 [VERIFIED-1]
flair_2: Paul Bloom — Against Empathy: The Case for Rational Compassion (Ecco, 2016) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Against_Empathy [VERIFIED-1]
notes: Strauss: compassion = recognising suffering + feeling for + tolerating + motivation to act; that last element is what separates this row from Affective Empathy (D1-3). OVERLAP with Warmth (A2-2): BFAS Compassion is the A-side aspect, Warmth the E-side facet. Bloom is the contrasting flair (empathy is a poor moral guide; compassion is not).

definition: Habit of doing considerate, generous things for others without being asked.
taxonomy: VIA Kindness (Humanity) · NEO-PI-R A3 Altruism content
formal_1: Peterson C & Seligman MEP (2004). Character Strengths and Virtues: A Handbook and Classification. New York: Oxford University Press / Washington DC: APA. [VERIFIED-1]
formal_2: Curry OS, Rowland LA, Van Lissa CJ, Zlotowitz S, McAlaney J & Whitehouse H (2018). Happy to help? A systematic review and meta-analysis of the effects of performing acts of kindness on the well-being of the actor. J Exp Soc Psychol 76:320-329. DOI:10.1016/j.jesp.2018.02.014 [VERIFIED-1]
formal_3: Rowland L & Curry OS (2019). A range of kindness activities boost happiness. J Soc Psychol 159(3):340-343. DOI:10.1080/00224545.2018.1469461 PMID:29702043 [VERIFIED-2]
flair_1: Psychology Today — Understanding Acts of Kindness — https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/emotional-nourishment/202406/understanding-acts-of-kindness [VERIFIED-1]
notes: Starting list "Kindness/Generosity" — named Kindness for the VIA strength; generosity is the L5 word. OVERLAP with Altruism (D4-5): Kindness = everyday considerate acts (VIA), Altruism = costly helping (Rushton). No widely validated adult kindness trait scale exists apart from the VIA-IS subscale; the Curry meta-analysis (intervention effects, delta = 0.28) is the nearest trait-specific evidence — flag if the assembler wants a scale paper. Curry 2018 not in PubMed (web route only).

definition: Tendency to catch and feel others' emotions, with other-oriented concern.
taxonomy: Davis IRI Empathic Concern · QCAE Affective Empathy · Mehrabian QMEE
formal_1: Davis MH (1983). Measuring individual differences in empathy: evidence for a multidimensional approach. J Pers Soc Psychol 44(1):113-126. DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.44.1.113 [VERIFIED-1]
formal_2: Mehrabian A & Epstein N (1972). A measure of emotional empathy. J Pers 40(4):525-543. DOI:10.1111/j.1467-6494.1972.tb00078.x PMID:4642390 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Reniers RLEP, Corcoran R, Drake R, Shryane NM & Völlm BA (2011). The QCAE: a Questionnaire of Cognitive and Affective Empathy. J Pers Assess 93(1):84-95. DOI:10.1080/00223891.2010.528484 PMID:21184334 [VERIFIED-2]
notes: Davis separates Empathic Concern (other-oriented) from Personal Distress (self-oriented); L6 is where the two merge. OVERLAP with Sentimentality (A3-6), which also cites Davis EC: A3-6 is the being-moved temperament, this row is the feeling-with mechanism. Davis 1983 is not indexed in PubMed (title search returned nothing) — DOI from publisher/index route.

definition: Habit of imagining how a situation looks from another person's point of view.
taxonomy: Davis IRI Perspective Taking · QCAE Cognitive Empathy · Basic Empathy Scale (cognitive)
formal_1: Davis MH (1983). Measuring individual differences in empathy: evidence for a multidimensional approach. J Pers Soc Psychol 44(1):113-126. DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.44.1.113 [VERIFIED-1]
formal_2: Reniers RLEP, Corcoran R, Drake R, Shryane NM & Völlm BA (2011). The QCAE: a Questionnaire of Cognitive and Affective Empathy. J Pers Assess 93(1):84-95. DOI:10.1080/00223891.2010.528484 PMID:21184334 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Jolliffe D & Farrington DP (2006). Development and validation of the Basic Empathy Scale. J Adolesc 29(4):589-611. DOI:10.1016/j.adolescence.2005.08.010 PMID:16198409 [VERIFIED-1]
flair_1: Greater Good Magazine — The Terms of Empathy — https://greatergood.berkeley.edu/article/item/the_terms_of_empathy [VERIFIED-1]
flair_2: Paul Bloom — Against Empathy: The Case for Rational Compassion (Ecco, 2016) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Against_Empathy [VERIFIED-1]
notes: Starting list "Cognitive Empathy/Perspective Taking" — named for the IRI subscale. Cognitive and affective empathy are separable in all three instruments (Davis, Reniers, Jolliffe) — that is the warrant for keeping D1-3 and D1-4 as two rows. Jolliffe & Farrington is an adolescent sample (PubMed route only for the second reader).

definition: Sympathy-leaning attitude; judging by feeling and mercy rather than hard-headed logic.
taxonomy: NEO-PI-R A6 Tender-Mindedness (James's tough-/tender-minded)
formal_1: Costa PT, McCrae RR & Dye DA (1991). Facet scales for agreeableness and conscientiousness: a revision of the NEO Personality Inventory. Pers Individ Dif 12(9):887-898. DOI:10.1016/0191-8869(91)90177-D [VERIFIED-1]
formal_2: Costa PT & McCrae RR (1995). Domains and facets: hierarchical personality assessment using the Revised NEO Personality Inventory. J Pers Assess 64(1):21-50. DOI:10.1207/s15327752jpa6401_2 PMID:16367732 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Axelrod SR, Widiger TA, Trull TJ & Corbitt EM (1997). Relations of five-factor model antagonism facets with personality disorder symptomatology. J Pers Assess 69(2):297-313. DOI:10.1207/s15327752jpa6902_4 PMID:9392892 [VERIFIED-2]
notes: Attitudinal facet, not a feeling: Compassion (D1-1) is the response to suffering, Tender-Mindedness the standing policy of mercy over justice. Contested: A6 is the weakest-loading Agreeableness facet (Costa 1991) and Axelrod 1997 found it converges with PD traits only on interview scores. Kept because no other row carries the tough/tender policy axis. Costa 1995 reused from col A (VERIFIED-2 there; PubMed re-run here).

definition: Drive to care for, protect and support those who depend on one.
taxonomy: Jackson PRF Nurturance (Murray nNur) · IAS-R Warm-Agreeable (LM) octant · Rushton twin nurturance scale
formal_1: Jackson DN (1984). Personality Research Form Manual (3rd ed.). Port Huron MI: Research Psychologists Press / Sigma Assessment Systems. [VERIFIED-1]
formal_2: Rushton JP, Fulker DW, Neale MC, Nias DKB & Eysenck HJ (1986). Altruism and aggression: the heritability of individual differences. J Pers Soc Psychol 50(6):1192-1198. DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.50.6.1192 PMID:3723334 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Wiggins JS, Trapnell P & Phillips N (1988). Psychometric and geometric characteristics of the revised Interpersonal Adjective Scales (IAS-R). Multivariate Behav Res 23(4):517-530. DOI:10.1207/s15327906mbr2304_8 PMID:26761163 [VERIFIED-2]
notes: Rushton 1986 is the trait-specific evidence: a nurturance questionnaire in 573 adult twin pairs (broad heritability reported ~70%, ~50% after model-fitting — quoted from the abstract, not re-run). PRF manual publisher name confirmed only as current Sigma Assessment Systems (web). Circumplex LM octant is nurturance in Wiggins's own vocabulary.

definition: Generalized expectation that other people's words and intentions can be relied upon.
taxonomy: NEO-PI-R A1 Trust · Rotter Interpersonal Trust Scale · Yamagishi general trust · Evans & Revelle Propensity to Trust
formal_1: Rotter JB (1967). A new scale for the measurement of interpersonal trust. J Pers 35(4):651-665. DOI:10.1111/j.1467-6494.1967.tb01454.x PMID:4865583 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Yamagishi T & Yamagishi M (1994). Trust and commitment in the United States and Japan. Motiv Emot 18(2):129-166. DOI:10.1007/BF02249397 [VERIFIED-1]
formal_3: Thielmann I & Hilbig BE (2015). Trust: an integrative review from a person-situation perspective. Rev Gen Psychol 19(3):249-277. DOI:10.1037/gpr0000046 [VERIFIED-1]
notes: Also Evans AM & Revelle W (2008). Survey and behavioral measurements of interpersonal trust. J Res Pers 42:1585-1593. DOI:10.1016/j.jrp.2008.07.011 [VERIFIED-1]. Yamagishi separates trust (a bias under uncertainty) from assurance (incentive structures) — L4/L5 are trust proper. L6 "gullible" is a level word I assigned [MINE]; Rotter argued high trust is not gullibility.

definition: Readiness to work with others toward joint outcomes rather than for oneself alone.
taxonomy: Cloninger TCI Cooperativeness · Van Lange social value orientation (prosocial)
formal_1: Cloninger CR, Svrakic DM & Przybeck TR (1993). A psychobiological model of temperament and character. Arch Gen Psychiatry 50(12):975-990. DOI:10.1001/archpsyc.1993.01820240059008 PMID:8250684 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Van Lange PAM, Otten W, De Bruin EMN & Joireman JA (1997). Development of prosocial, individualistic, and competitive orientations: theory and preliminary evidence. J Pers Soc Psychol 73(4):733-746. DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.73.4.733 PMID:9325591 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Balliet D, Parks C & Joireman J (2009). Social value orientation and cooperation in social dilemmas: a meta-analysis. Group Process Intergroup Relat 12(4):533-547. DOI:10.1177/1368430209105040 [VERIFIED-1]
flair_1: Psychology Today — Cooperation and Human Nature — https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/am-i-right/201304/cooperation-and-human-nature [VERIFIED-1]
notes: TCI Cooperativeness is a character dimension bundling social acceptance, empathy, helpfulness, compassion and principledness — OVERLAP with Tolerance (D2-5), which TCI files as its C1 subscale. SVO is the game-theoretic reading; Balliet: SVO-cooperation r = .30 (quoted). Cloninger 1993 reused from col A (VERIFIED-2 there; PubMed re-run here).

definition: Disposition to release resentment and revenge motives after being wronged.
taxonomy: McCullough TRIM · Berry Trait Forgivingness Scale · Thompson Heartland Forgiveness Scale · HEXACO A Forgiveness
formal_1: McCullough ME, Rachal KC, Sandage SJ, Worthington EL, Brown SW & Hight TL (1998). Interpersonal forgiving in close relationships: II. Theoretical elaboration and measurement. J Pers Soc Psychol 75(6):1586-1603. DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.75.6.1586 PMID:9914668 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Berry JW, Worthington EL, O'Connor LE, Parrott L & Wade NG (2005). Forgivingness, vengeful rumination, and affective traits. J Pers 73(1):183-225. DOI:10.1111/j.1467-6494.2004.00308.x PMID:15660677 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Fehr R, Gelfand MJ & Nag M (2010). The road to forgiveness: a meta-analytic synthesis of its situational and dispositional correlates. Psychol Bull 136(5):894-914. DOI:10.1037/a0019993 PMID:20804242 [VERIFIED-2]
notes: Also Thompson LY et al (2005). Dispositional forgiveness of self, others, and situations. J Pers 73(2):313-359. DOI:10.1111/j.1467-6494.2005.00311.x PMID:15745433 [VERIFIED-1]. Fehr: situational variables (apology, intent, state empathy) explain more of single-episode forgiveness than dispositions — this row is the disposition (Berry's "forgivingness"). Greater Good: forgiving is not condoning or reconciling — L6 is where that line is lost.

definition: Tendency in conflict to yield, inhibit aggression and keep the peace rather than fight.
taxonomy: NEO-PI-R A4 Compliance · Rahim ROCI-II obliging style · HEXACO A Flexibility
formal_1: Graziano WG, Jensen-Campbell LA & Hair EC (1996). Perceiving interpersonal conflict and reacting to it: the case for agreeableness. J Pers Soc Psychol 70(4):820-835. DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.70.4.820 PMID:8636901 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Jensen-Campbell LA & Graziano WG (2001). Agreeableness as a moderator of interpersonal conflict. J Pers 69(2):323-361. DOI:10.1111/1467-6494.00148 PMID:11339802 [VERIFIED-1]
formal_3: Rahim MA (1983). A measure of styles of handling interpersonal conflict. Acad Manage J 26(2):368-376. DOI:10.5465/255985 PMID:10263067 [VERIFIED-2]
notes: Starting list "Compliance/Agreeableness". The D4 starting trait "Deference/Agreeableness-in-conflict" is the same NEO A4 content, so it is FOLDED into this row and D4-2 became Gentleness (see there). Graziano: low-A people rate power assertion as a better conflict tactic — L1/L2. Also Costa, McCrae & Dye 1991 [VERIFIED-1]. Axelrod 1997: Compliance was the one antagonism facet that did not track PD symptoms.

definition: Acceptance of, and respect for, people and ways of life different from one's own.
taxonomy: Hjerm tolerance scale (acceptance / respect / appreciation) · TCI Cooperativeness C1 Social Acceptance · Sibley & Duckitt prejudice (inverse)
formal_1: Hjerm M, Eger MA, Bohman A & Fors Connolly F (2020). A new approach to the study of tolerance: conceptualizing and measuring acceptance, respect, and appreciation of difference. Soc Indic Res 147(3):897-919. DOI:10.1007/s11205-019-02176-y [VERIFIED-1]
formal_2: Sibley CG & Duckitt J (2008). Personality and prejudice: a meta-analysis and theoretical review. Pers Soc Psychol Rev 12(3):248-279. DOI:10.1177/1088868308319226 PMID:18641385 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Cloninger CR, Svrakic DM & Przybeck TR (1993). A psychobiological model of temperament and character. Arch Gen Psychiatry 50(12):975-990. DOI:10.1001/archpsyc.1993.01820240059008 PMID:8250684 [VERIFIED-2]
notes: Contested: tolerance is usually measured as an attitude, not a personality trait. Hjerm's three dimensions supply L2 (acceptance), L4 (respect), L5 (appreciation). Sibley & Duckitt anchor it in personality by the inverse: prejudice is predicted by low Agreeableness (via SDO) and low Openness (via RWA), N = 22,068 (quoted). OVERLAP with an Openness column if it carries open-mindedness.

definition: Frankness and sincerity in dealing with others; not manipulating or flattering to get one's way.
taxonomy: NEO-PI-R A2 Straightforwardness · HEXACO H Sincerity · Machiavellianism (inverse)
formal_1: Costa PT, McCrae RR & Dye DA (1991). Facet scales for agreeableness and conscientiousness: a revision of the NEO Personality Inventory. Pers Individ Dif 12(9):887-898. DOI:10.1016/0191-8869(91)90177-D [VERIFIED-1]
formal_2: Axelrod SR, Widiger TA, Trull TJ & Corbitt EM (1997). Relations of five-factor model antagonism facets with personality disorder symptomatology. J Pers Assess 69(2):297-313. DOI:10.1207/s15327752jpa6902_4 PMID:9392892 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Ashton MC, Lee K & de Vries RE (2014). The HEXACO Honesty-Humility, Agreeableness, and Emotionality factors: a review of research and theory. Pers Soc Psychol Rev 18(2):139-152. DOI:10.1177/1088868314523838 PMID:24577101 [VERIFIED-1]
notes: The L5/L6 tension with Politeness (D4-6) is by design: the two rows pull against each other and a persona needs both dials. Axelrod: straightforwardness converged with antisocial traits even on self-report. HEXACO moves this content from A to Honesty-Humility — OVERLAP with any Honesty/Integrity row in another column. Also Costa & McCrae 1995 [VERIFIED-2].

definition: Comfort with closeness and confidence that others will be there; low anxiety and low avoidance.
taxonomy: Brennan/Clark/Shaver ECR · Fraley ECR-R · Hazan & Shaver three-style typology
formal_1: Brennan KA, Clark CL & Shaver PR (1998). Self-report measurement of adult attachment: an integrative overview. In Simpson JA & Rholes WS (eds) Attachment Theory and Close Relationships, pp 46-76. New York: Guilford. [VERIFIED-1]
formal_2: Fraley RC, Waller NG & Brennan KA (2000). An item response theory analysis of self-report measures of adult attachment. J Pers Soc Psychol 78(2):350-365. DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.78.2.350 PMID:10707340 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Hazan C & Shaver P (1987). Romantic love conceptualized as an attachment process. J Pers Soc Psychol 52(3):511-524. DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.52.3.511 PMID:3572722 [VERIFIED-2]
notes: Two ECR dimensions (anxiety, avoidance) collapsed into one bipolar row; L2 therefore forks (clingy = anxious, distant = avoidant) — assembler may prefer two rows. Insecure styles are normal variation, not diagnoses. Levine & Heller not confirmed by either route before the search budget expired (Wikipedia fetch returned empty).

definition: Strength of the desire to be accepted and included by other people.
L6: desperate to belong, crushed by rejection
neighbors: Gregariousness (col A) · Social Connectedness · Attachment Security
taxonomy: Leary Need to Belong Scale · Baumeister & Leary belongingness hypothesis · trait affiliation (DeYoung)
formal_1: Baumeister RF & Leary MR (1995). The need to belong: desire for interpersonal attachments as a fundamental human motivation. Psychol Bull 117(3):497-529. DOI:10.1037/0033-2909.117.3.497 PMID:7777651 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Leary MR, Kelly KM, Cottrell CA & Schreindorfer LS (2013). Construct validity of the Need to Belong Scale: mapping the nomological network. J Pers Assess 95(6):610-624. DOI:10.1080/00223891.2013.819511 PMID:23905716 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: DeYoung CG, Weisberg YJ, Quilty LC & Peterson JB (2013). Unifying the aspects of the Big Five, the interpersonal circumplex, and trait affiliation. J Pers 81(5):465-475. DOI:10.1111/jopy.12020 PMID:23126539 [VERIFIED-2]
flair_1: Greater Good Magazine — Social Connection Definition — https://greatergood.berkeley.edu/topic/social_connection/definition [VERIFIED-1]
notes: Leary 2013 (nine studies): need to belong correlates with but is distinct from extraversion and affiliation motivation, and is NOT the same as insecure attachment — so D3-2 is not a duplicate of D3-1 or of Gregariousness (A2-1). Baumeister & Leary 1995 PMID has no DOI in PubMed; DOI from the APA/web route.

definition: Steadfast commitment to one's own people and groups, kept when it costs something.
L3: sticks by own in a pinch
taxonomy: Moral Foundations Questionnaire Ingroup/Loyalty · VIA Teamwork (loyalty component) · OCB loyal boosterism
formal_1: Graham J, Nosek BA, Haidt J, Iyer R, Koleva S & Ditto PH (2011). Mapping the moral domain. J Pers Soc Psychol 101(2):366-385. DOI:10.1037/a0021847 PMID:21244182 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Hildreth JAD, Gino F & Bazerman M (2016). Blind loyalty? When group loyalty makes us see evil or engage in it. Organ Behav Hum Decis Process 132:16-36. DOI:10.1016/j.obhdp.2015.10.001 [VERIFIED-1]
formal_3: Peterson C & Seligman MEP (2004). Character Strengths and Virtues: A Handbook and Classification. New York: Oxford University Press / Washington DC: APA. [VERIFIED-1]
flair_1: Forbes / HBS Working Knowledge — Is Loyalty a Force for Good or Evil? — https://www.forbes.com/sites/hbsworkingknowledge/2016/01/11/is-loyalty-a-force-for-good-or-evil-research-reveals-it-can-be-both/ [VERIFIED-1]
notes: CONTESTED: no validated adult personality scale named "loyalty" was found (PubMed title search returned nothing); the MFQ Loyalty foundation measures it as a moral concern, VIA folds it into Teamwork, and Hildreth is the trait-specific experimental evidence (loyalty cuts cheating except under high competition — which supplies L6). Assembler may prefer to treat this as a value, not a trait.

definition: Skill at reading people and situations and acting effectively on what one reads.
neighbors: Perspective Taking · Politeness · Social Boldness (col A)
taxonomy: VIA Social Intelligence · Tromsø Social Intelligence Scale (TSIS)
formal_1: Silvera DH, Martinussen M & Dahl TI (2001). The Tromsø Social Intelligence Scale, a self-report measure of social intelligence. Scand J Psychol 42(4):313-319. DOI:10.1111/1467-9450.00242 PMID:11547906 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Kihlstrom JF & Cantor N (2000). Social intelligence. In Sternberg RJ (ed) Handbook of Intelligence (2nd ed), pp 359-379. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. [VERIFIED-1]
formal_3: Peterson C & Seligman MEP (2004). Character Strengths and Virtues: A Handbook and Classification. New York: Oxford University Press / Washington DC: APA. [VERIFIED-1]
flair_1: Greater Good Magazine — Social Connection Definition (quotes Goleman's Social Intelligence) — https://greatergood.berkeley.edu/topic/social_connection/definition [VERIFIED-1]
flair_2: Daniel Goleman — Social Intelligence: The New Science of Human Relationships (Bantam, 2006) [UNVERIFIED]
notes: TSIS has three factors (social information processing, social skills, social awareness). Contested (Kihlstrom & Cantor): social intelligence is hard to separate psychometrically from g and from personality. L6 shades into Machiavellianism — a dark-side column should own that. Goleman book not confirmed (Wikipedia fetch empty); left as UNVERIFIED.

definition: Willingness to do one's share and go beyond it for the group or organisation.
taxonomy: VIA Teamwork/Citizenship · Organ organizational citizenship behaviour (OCB)
formal_1: Organ DW & Ryan K (1995). A meta-analytic review of attitudinal and dispositional predictors of organizational citizenship behavior. Pers Psychol 48(4):775-802. DOI:10.1111/j.1744-6570.1995.tb01781.x [VERIFIED-1]
formal_2: Chiaburu DS, Oh IS, Berry CM, Li N & Gardner RG (2011). The five-factor model of personality traits and organizational citizenship behaviors: a meta-analysis. J Appl Psychol 96(6):1140-1166. DOI:10.1037/a0024004 PMID:21688883 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Peterson C & Seligman MEP (2004). Character Strengths and Virtues: A Handbook and Classification. New York: Oxford University Press / Washington DC: APA. [VERIFIED-1]
notes: Starting list "Teamwork/Citizenship" — named Teamwork (VIA). OCB is a behaviour class, not a trait; Chiaburu (87 samples) shows A and C are its established trait predictors, with Emotional Stability, E and O adding incremental validity — the warrant for a trait row. OVERLAP with a Conscientiousness column (dutifulness).

definition: Enduring sense of closeness to and belonging with the social world; the inverse of trait loneliness.
neighbors: Need To Belong · Attachment Security · Gregariousness (col A)
taxonomy: Lee & Robbins Social Connectedness Scale · UCLA Loneliness Scale v3 (inverse)
formal_1: Lee RM & Robbins SB (1995). Measuring belongingness: the Social Connectedness and the Social Assurance scales. J Couns Psychol 42(2):232-241. DOI:10.1037/0022-0167.42.2.232 [VERIFIED-1]
formal_2: Russell DW (1996). UCLA Loneliness Scale (Version 3): reliability, validity, and factor structure. J Pers Assess 66(1):20-40. DOI:10.1207/s15327752jpa6601_2 PMID:8576833 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Hawkley LC & Cacioppo JT (2010). Loneliness matters: a theoretical and empirical review of consequences and mechanisms. Ann Behav Med 40(2):218-227. DOI:10.1007/s12160-010-9210-8 PMID:20652462 [VERIFIED-2]
flair_2: Greater Good Magazine — Social Connection Definition — https://greatergood.berkeley.edu/topic/social_connection/definition [VERIFIED-1]
notes: Starting list "Loneliness-proneness (or Social Connectedness)" — named for the positive pole; loneliness is L1/L2. Russell: UCLA-3 fits a single bipolar factor, so one row is honest. Also Buecker S, Maes M, Denissen JJA & Luhmann M (2020). Loneliness and the Big Five personality traits: a meta-analysis. Eur J Pers 34(1):8-28. DOI:10.1002/per.2229 [VERIFIED-1] (E r = -.37, N r = .36, quoted). OVERLAP with Need To Belong: desire (D3-2) vs felt state (D3-6).

definition: Drive to control, lead and prevail over others in interaction.
taxonomy: IAS-R Assured-Dominant (PA) octant · PRF Dominance · Cheng dominance-vs-prestige
formal_1: Wiggins JS, Trapnell P & Phillips N (1988). Psychometric and geometric characteristics of the revised Interpersonal Adjective Scales (IAS-R). Multivariate Behav Res 23(4):517-530. DOI:10.1207/s15327906mbr2304_8 PMID:26761163 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Cheng JT, Tracy JL, Foulsham T, Kingstone A & Henrich J (2013). Two ways to the top: evidence that dominance and prestige are distinct yet viable avenues to social rank and influence. J Pers Soc Psychol 104(1):103-125. DOI:10.1037/a0030398 PMID:23163747 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_3: Jackson DN (1984). Personality Research Form Manual (3rd ed.). Port Huron MI: Research Psychologists Press / Sigma Assessment Systems. [VERIFIED-1]
flair_1: Joseph Henrich lab — Prestige (research topic page) — https://henrich.fas.harvard.edu/research-topics-new/prestige [VERIFIED-1]
notes: OVERLAP with Assertiveness (A2-3): NEO E3 is the speaking-up facet, this row is the circumplex agency axis (control over others). Cheng: dominance (fear) and prestige (respect) both buy rank but only dominance costs liking — L5/L6 are the dominance strategy, not prestige. Also Wiggins 1979 JPSP 37:395-412 DOI:10.1037/0022-3514.37.3.395 [VERIFIED-1] and Horowitz IIP 1988 PMID:3204198 [VERIFIED-1].

definition: Leniency in judging and treating others; mild rather than harsh or critical.
taxonomy: HEXACO Agreeableness: Gentleness facet
formal_1: Ashton MC & Lee K (2007). Empirical, theoretical, and practical advantages of the HEXACO model of personality structure. Pers Soc Psychol Rev 11(2):150-166. DOI:10.1177/1088868306294907 PMID:18453460 [VERIFIED-2]
formal_2: Ashton MC, Lee K & de Vries RE (2014). The HEXACO Honesty-Humility, Agreeableness, and Emotionality factors: a review of research and theory. Pers Soc Psychol Rev 18(2):139-152. DOI:10.1177/1088868314523838 PMID:24577101 [VERIFIED-1]
formal_3: Lee K & Ashton MC (2004). Psychometric properties of the HEXACO Personality Inventory. Multivariate Behav Res 39(2):329-358. DOI:10.1207/s15327906mbr3902_8 [VERIFIED-1]
